description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of twelve distinct subject domains, representing the domain distribution of the annotated AttrEval-GenSearch test set. The chart is divided into twelve slices, with category labels and their corresponding percentages positioned outside the pie and connected to each segment via thin grey lines. There is no separate legend; instead, the labels feature black text for the category names with grey text for the percentages directly below them. Starting from the top right and moving clockwise, the largest slice is "AI/NLP Research" in blue at 24.3%, followed by "Business" in red at 5.9%, "Geography" in yellow-gold at 2.7%, and "Math" in green at 1.2%. Continuing clockwise, "Game&Anime" is colored orange (8.2%), "Econ. & Fin." is teal (18.4%), "Science" is light blue (6.7%), and "Law" is light red (5.1%). The remaining slices are "History" in yellow (8.2%), "Med & Health" in light green (6.7%), "Pet & Animal" in light orange (5.5%), and "Daily Life" in light cyan (7.1%). The segments do not appear to be arranged in any specific size-based order, such as ascending or descending, and none of the slices are visually emphasized, exploded, or offset.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the domain distribution of the annotated AttrEval-GenSearch test set, encompassing twelve distinct categories. The largest category, 'AI/NLP Research,' accounts for approximately 24.3% of the dataset, followed by 'Econ. & Fin.' at 18.4%. 'History' and 'Game&Anime' are tied at 8.2%, while 'Daily Life' constitutes 7.1%. 'Med & Health' and 'Science' both represent 6.7%, with 'Business' slightly lower at 5.9%. 'Pet & Animal' and 'Law' are close in proportion, at 5.5% and 5.1%, respectively. 'Geography' and 'Math' are the smallest categories, with 'Geography' at 3.7% and 'Math' at 2.2%. Notably, 'Daily Life' has shown a consistent increase in representation compared to previous datasets, while 'Geography' has seen a slight decline.
